review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the definitions of nfCoeff, nfExponent, termOrder and dominantIndices in Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_UVCrossingDominantIndices.lean. The file has no simp-loop risk and no competing rewrite rules that I could see. The only simp-attribute use is the four @[scoped simp] lemmas on nfCoeff and nfExponent. The findings are about missing or inconsistent simp coverage. I did not run Lean, so I can't say whether the proposed attributes would clash with the existing simp set in any particular call. In particular, ij is a reducible abbrev, so simp may already see through it to Finsupp.add_apply. Both findings are therefore moderate in strength.

findings.excerpt:
theorem ij_apply_zero (i j : ℕ) : ij i j 0 = i := by simp [ij]
theorem ij_apply_one (i j : ℕ) : ij i j 1 = j := by simp [ij]
findings.problem: These are the canonical evaluation lemmas for the file's coordinate constructor `ij`. They have no @[simp] attribute, so every caller names them by hand. They appear in about ten simp/rw calls (lines 170, 214, 217, 238, 244, 253, 369, 407, 413). Elsewhere the file falls back to `simp [ij]` (lines 106, 130, 135), which unfolds the abbrev into Finsupp.single sums and leaves goals in a different normal form. The simp interface for `ij` is therefore inconsistent: sometimes the named lemmas, sometimes unfolding.
findings.proposed_change: Mark both lemmas @[simp]. Since `ij` is a reducible abbrev, the discrimination tree may index the LHS through its unfolding. If so, the attribute would overlap with Finsupp.add_apply and Finsupp.single_apply rather than add a new rule, so check that. Then replace the explicit `ij_apply_zero, ij_apply_one` arguments in the simp/simp only calls with the default simp set, and keep `simp [ij]` only where full unfolding is wanted.
findings.benefit: Calls such as `simp [coeff_inU, coeff_inV, ij_apply_zero, ij_apply_one]` and the three long `simp only [...] at h` blocks in normalForm_unique get shorter. Goals about coefficients at `ij i j` reduce to the plain `i`/`j` form without unfolding `ij`.

findings.declaration: SlopeLawSol.termOrder_natCast / termOrder_negSucc (with scoped simp lemmas nfCoeff_*, nfExponent_*)
findings.excerpt:
theorem termOrder_natCast (v : W → ℕ∞) (E t : ℕ) (ab : PowerSeries W × PowerSeries W) (i : ℕ) :
    termOrder v E t ab (i : ℤ) = v (PowerSeries.coeff i ab.1) + ((i * t : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by
  simp [termOrder, annulusWeight]
findings.problem: The file gives nfCoeff and nfExponent a @[scoped simp] interface on the two constructor forms `(i : ℤ)` and `Int.negSucc j`, but stops one level short. The next definition, `termOrder`, has the analogous lemmas termOrder_natCast and termOrder_negSucc with no simp attribute. Callers then work around this. The `rw [termOrder]` calls at lines 799, 1149 and 1253 unfold it into `v (nfCoeff ab n) + ↑(annulusWeight ..)`. Line 1149 then needs a `change` to put the goal back in a usable shape. Other places call `rw [termOrder_natCast]` or `rw [termOrder_negSucc]` explicitly (e.g. in dominantIndices_bddBelow and dominantIndices_bddAbove). So the normal form for `termOrder ... (i : ℤ)` is not what simp produces, even though the lemma stating it exists.
findings.proposed_change: Mark termOrder_natCast and termOrder_negSucc @[scoped simp], matching the four lemmas above them. Alternatively, put all six lemmas as plain @[simp] in the definitions file next to nfCoeff, nfExponent and termOrder. The scoped lemmas are currently only visible inside SlopeLawSol, and the same name set appears in many sibling Sol files. Then use `simp` in place of the manual `rw [termOrder_natCast]`/`rw [termOrder]; change ...` steps.
findings.benefit: Terms of the form `termOrder v E t ab (i : ℤ)` or `termOrder v E t ab (Int.negSucc j)` would rewrite directly to the coefficient-plus-weight normal form. That would remove the manual unfolding and `change` steps in iInf_termOrder_lt_top and exists_nfCoeff_ne_top. It would also make the simp interface consistent across the nfCoeff, nfExponent and termOrder layers.
